Gertrude Stein, Three Lives.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/gertrude-stein/three-lives

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Gertrude Stein, the author, died 1946 (Wikidata Q188385, P570 = 1946-07-27).

First publication of the text used: 1909 (SE colophon: 'Three Lives was published in 1909 by Gertrude Stein.'). Wikipedia says that Stein had the Grafton Press of New York print the book at her own expense.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in New York in 1909, before 1931, so the United States rule settles the country of origin. The edition's own statement of rights, quoted below, says the text is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (United States): the text was first published in the United States before 1931, so no other country's term applies. The last person to die, Gertrude Stein, died in 1946, which does not change this.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: 'Three Lives was published in 1909 by Gertrude Stein.'
- Wikipedia, 'Three Lives (book)', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three_Lives_(book): Stein's friend found 'the vanity publisher Grafton Press of New York; Stein had the firm print Three Lives at her own expense'.
- Wikidata Q188385 (Gertrude Stein), P570 = 1946-07-27.
